notes.text:
Theorem 11 and exact native197 n4 of whole255 asserted a false global uniform-continuity guarantee. Whole255/200 remains FAIL.

On the saturated unit-weight balanced line, take actual gamma(x)=|x|, A_n(x)=|x−2n| and B_n(x)=|x−2n−1/(8n)|. Their slopes are integral ±1 and constants rational on finite rational carrying subdivisions. Ambient convexity proves printed rational-endpoint PCC inequalities. Their relative norms are 2n and 2n+1/(8n); both recession slopes are 1. They are genuine literal PA regularizable endpoints. Primitive recursion cancels at affine/artificial vertices and gives outgoing slopes 1,1 at each kink, hence MA(A_n)=2delta_(2n), MA(B_n)=2delta_(2n+1/(8n)). Their uniform distance is 1/(8n). For the single fixed C_b test sin(pi x²), the absolute evaluation difference is 2cos(pi/(64n²)), tending to 2.

For even n, set a_j=4j+(j mod 2), b_j=4j+1−(j mod 2), and average |x−a_j| and |x−b_j| over 0≤j<n. These are actual convex rational-affine PA_R functions on finite rational subdivisions, with outer slopes ±1 and bounded difference from gamma. Raw measures are (2/n)sum delta_a and (2/n)sum delta_b, each mass 2. Each consecutive pair produces a disjoint trapezoidal difference of height 2 before division by n; therefore the uniform distance is exactly 2/n. The continuous eight-periodic interpolation through (0,1/4),(1,−1/4),(4,−1/4),(5,1/4),(8,1/4) has sup norm 1/4 and Lipschitz constant 1/2. Its values at every a_j,b_j are 1/4,−1/4, giving measure difference exactly 1. This disproves global BL uniform continuity, including the summed-norm BL convention.

Both averaged relative norms equal 2n−3/2. These families have no common fixed relative bound and do not converge uniformly to one relative endpoint. The correction is material, not terminology.

The genuine raw divisor is D_f c(tau)=sum c_sigma f_sigma(n_sigma/tau)−f_tau(sum c_sigma n_sigma/tau), using saturated primitive inward quotient normals. notes.text:

Define gamma=max(|x|,|y|,|z|)+|z| and f=max(|x|,|y|−1,|z|)+|z|. They are ambient convex literal PA restrictions on rational geometry, −1≤f−gamma≤0, and gamma≥max|coordinates| proves positive growth.

On the horizontal plane, h(a,b)=max(|a|,|b|)+|b| has first weight 2 on each a-axis ray and 1 on each of four primitive diagonals. Opposing transverse lifts give axis weight 2; diagonal gradient differences evaluated on determinant-one lifts give weight 1. The b-axis has zero weight. Outgoing slopes 1 and 2 give origin mass 12. On the vertical plane, max(|y|−1,|z|)+|z| has central-axis weight 4, outer-axis weights 2 and graph-ray weights 1. At p_±=(0,±1,0), primitive directions have weights 4,2,1,1 and slopes 0,1,2,2, yielding mass 6 each. They balance. All other walls and the artificially subdivided central origin contribute zero. Hence MA(gamma)=24delta_0 and MA(f)=12delta_0+6delta_p++6delta_p−. Polygon areas are independent checks, not operator definitions.

For R=1/4, u=f−gamma+(R−rho)_+ is literal bounded PA. Flat rational endpoints (0,±R,0), radial chords and shrinking rational simplices prove the unrestricted envelope is f. Its only roof atom is the origin, so contact is −3. At horizontal product corners, f and gamma have mixed difference −R; u has mixed difference R. This excludes precisely F(cross)+H(z), without a claim about arbitrary reparametrizations. The old separable endpoint remains failed data.

For an actual rational-affine positive-growth reference and a rational point v, take a rational homogeneous PC PA jet h on a specified rational tangent refinement. A slow rational ambient norm gives Psi=max(gamma,C+epsilon rho(x−v)), norm-active near v and gamma-active outside a compact set. Insert C+t+delta h by a maximum inside a rational star, choosing delta|h|≤epsilon rho/2 and t<epsilon r/4. The annular collar is unchanged. Local supports prove PC, all equality walls are rational, and bounded difference from the ACTUAL reference persists. The germ is exactly C+t+delta h; flat costs scale by delta and raw atom by delta^d. This is real-category gluing, not literal gluing.

For a real bad jet on a fixed rational refinement, shared-face and PC constraints are rational linear. A flat relation gives a rational extreme zero-cost equation. Rational approximation within the active feasible face preserves all inequalities; positivity of the actual mass polynomial persists by continuity, also for specified positive real weights. Therefore every finite bad jet has an actual global realization in this reference scope. Finite-PA contact is equivalent to flat PC jets having zero raw atom at every rational point and every rational refinement. This gives no refinement bound or general non-PA sufficiency.

notes.text:
Fix finite pure positive balanced rational embedded X, ACTUAL rational-affine PA PC gamma positive at infinity, and raw M=deg(gamma). For each category *=Z,R, D_*(gamma) is only the uniform closure of actual relative PAPC_* functions on finite rational geometry. Merely continuous PC membership adds no endpoint. If M=0, positivity makes every output zero and the completion and continuity statements are immediate.

On a balanced finite one-cycle, bounded PA functions have zero slopes on unbounded edges. A bounded primitive-length-L edge contributes weight·(b(v)−b(w))(c(w)−c(v))/L to integral b D_c, symmetrically. Outgoing degree terms cancel. Replacing relative mixed factors by gamma preserves mass M and supplies bounded-difference IBP.

A compact ambient rational PA test psi has a finite rational wall arrangement. A sufficiently large rational K makes H0=Ksum|L_j| and H0+psi ambient convex. Choose rational epsilon slower than the actual reference recession growth, and raise A+epsilon H0 above gamma near the test support. Then theta0=max(gamma,A+epsilon H0) and theta1=theta0+epsilon psi are actual relative rational-affine REAL PA PC functions with theta1−theta0=epsilon psi. Their local support descriptions cover ties and collars; the slow term is inactive at infinity. Rational reference coefficients keep all walls rational. These auxiliaries need not be literal, but their finite real raw recursion is legitimate for either approximation category. No irrational-reference maximum closure is inferred.

Compact rational PA restrictions are uniformly dense in C_c with controlled supports, using finite rational centers and rational heights in max_j(a_j−Lrho(x−v_j))_+. Uniform continuity controls nearby bumps, distant bumps vanish, and signed functions are split into positive and negative parts. Supports can remain inside a prescribed open equality set.

Telescoping and primitive IBP give, for every fixed rational test psi, |integral psi(MA(a)−MA(b))|≤(2M/epsilon_psi)sum_i||a_i−b_i||_infinity. This constant is independent of both relative bounds. Uniform-Cauchy approximants therefore have Cauchy C_c evaluations. Their positive limiting functional has a unique finite Radon representation. The paper reconstructs open-set suprema, compact partitions, metric outer measure, closed-set measurability through alternating dyadic distance shells, regularity, and range-step integral representation; no broad source extension theorem is imported.

Preserve gamma and choose one fixed rational c with H=gamma+c≥0, proper. Let J=integral H MA(gamma), finite because the reference measure has finite support. Actual rational PA functions q_j=max(gamma−j,−c) satisfy gamma−q_j=min(H,j). For finite tuples bounded relatively by D, relative IBP and replacement of each factor by gamma give integral min(H,j) MA(a)≤2dDM+J. Increasing j proves common moments and tails. Every particular uniformly convergent family has a common finite D; compact cutoffs then prove exact limiting mass M and convergence against every C_b test.

Comparing arbitrary approximants proves sequence independence, and the same compact-test estimate passes to completed tuples. For EACH FIXED finite C, all tuples in F_*,C={f in D_*^d:max_i||f_i−gamma||≤C} satisfy integral H MA(f)≤K_C=2dCM+J and MA(f){H>T}≤K_C/T. Approximation bounds C+o(1) and compact truncation prove this for every completed tuple in the entire fixed-C family.

The vague uniformity uses finite C_c evaluation lists. Compact approximation costs at most 2M eta, followed by the fixed test estimate, so the map is GLOBALLY uniformly continuous for that uniformity. The weak C_b uniformity uses finite C_b evaluation lists. ONLY on F_*,C, cutting off a fixed test g and approximating the compact test gives |integral g(MA(f)−MA(h))|≤2||g||K_C/T+2M eta+L_psi sum_i||f_i−h_i||. Choosing T, eta and then input distance proves fixed-C weak uniform continuity. A radius-one neighborhood of a single tuple has C_f=1+max_i||f_i−gamma||, proving ordinary weak C_b continuity for sequences and nets.

For d_BL with sup norm≤1 and Lip≤1, a finite spatial mesh and value quantization give a finite uniform net on the compact cutoff support. Choose actual global representatives, cut off and rationally approximate finitely many tests, and take their largest test constant. The bound 2K_C/T+4M eta+Lmax·input distance proves BL uniform continuity ON THE FIXED-C FAMILY. No entire-domain weak or BL modulus remains, by n1.

Symmetry passes from raw recursion. Locality uses compact tests inside the equality set and local approximation errors. Finite constant sequences recover raw endpoints. Extract approximants with error≤2^−n and add rational 4·2^−n; consecutive drops are at least 2·2^−n−(2^−n+2^(−n−1))=2^(−n−1)>0. Thus uniform completion equals the declared decreasing domain, separately in each category.

For uniformly convergent actual C_b obstacles, contact integrals converge WHEN their envelopes have this proved domain membership. R230 gives uniform envelope convergence and a common relative bound from obstacle norms; weak C_b convergence and uniform gap convergence then suffice. This stability does not establish missing all-obstacle membership.

notes.text:

Chord error is (t−t_j)(t_j+1/N−t)/2, with maximum 1/(8N²). Dyadic chords decrease. The resulting F_N are actual relative rational-affine PA_R PC functions on rational geometry and decrease uniformly to F, supplying n4's genuine operator antecedent.

On the positive yz side put t_j=1+j/N, b_j=a_N(t_j), Delta_j=k_j−k_(j−1), k_−1=0,k_N=1. The initial atom is 6Delta_0. Initial first weights are 4 centrally, 2 outward and 1/q along primitive graph directions (q,±p), k_0=p/q; balances and outgoing slopes give the atom. For j=1,...,N, atoms are 4Delta_j at (t_j,0) and Delta_j at each (t_j,±b_j). Axis first weights 2,2,Delta_j,Delta_j and slopes −k_left,k_right,1,1 give 4Delta_j. All remaining walls are affine zero-weight walls; artificial vertices on straight affine first edges cancel. The horizontal plane contributes 12delta_0 and the central vertical origin contributes zero. Endpoint half-jumps are included and sum Delta_j=1, so raw total is 24.

The compact Riemann sums and sequence independence give exactly MA_R(F)=12delta_0+sum_(s=±1) integral_1^2[4delta_(0,st,0)+delta_(0,st,(t−1)²/2)+delta_(0,st,−(t−1)²/2)]dt. These are parameter pushforward densities, not arclength. Total mass is 24; integral y²=28 and integral z²=1/5.

notes.text:
Let X be finite noncompact rational embedded and gamma literal PA PC positive at infinity; balancing is unnecessary. Choose rational x in a noncompact component and rational C>gamma(x). Set phi=max(gamma,C), D=phi−gamma. D is nonnegative literal PA with compact support. Refine to pointed rational carrying cells. D vanishes on every unbounded cell: bounded affinity gives zero recession slope, and its constant value along a recession ray eventually vanishes. A cell path from positive D to infinity forces a bounded positive-dimensional cell with nonzero integral gap slope k. Choose primitive w with k(w)≠0 and a rational segment of length L in that cell. For integer N>|k(w)|, f=gamma+D/N is relative real rational-affine PC.

At every carrying vertex v choose a common sufficiently large integer B so D(v)/N+B rho(y−v)≥D(y)/N globally. Incident slopes and positive distances to finitely many nonincident cells prove existence. The minimum of these cones and D is a bounded literal obstacle u_N, lies between D/N and D, matches D(v)/N at vertices and vanishes on unbounded cells. Thus f is a competitor.

Every other printed-PC competitor is bounded by f at vertices. Caller R230's rational cone argument, applied to homogenized pointed cells, gives rational vertex-plus-recession decompositions. Replacing small portions of a vertex coefficient by sufficiently far rational recession endpoints yields PCCs whose obstacle values equal f. Jensen gives q≤f at rational points; shrinking rational simplices give the bound at real centers. Therefore the unrestricted envelope is exactly f.

Its primitive slope is gamma_sigma(w)+k(w)/N, nonintegral. Midpoint comparison with monotone integral slopes gives distance at least L·dist(q0,Z)/4 from every literal PA PC approximant. Hence literal regularization fails and no literal MA is assigned to this endpoint.

Caller B225 excludes compact support only for nonempty finite pure positive balanced cycles globally embedded in one vector space, dimension≥1. In this fixed source category every positive-growth literal pair therefore fails the all-PA-obstacle regularity antecedent. This is not a measured contact claim. Abstract compact chart spaces retain their separate compatible-chart and finite-bounded-decomposition hypotheses.

In dimension zero, the envelope on a finite rational set is pointwise gamma+u for every C_b obstacle. It is real PA; irrational values also admit decreasing rational pointwise constants, uniformly because the set is finite. The genuine zero-fold measure is [X], independent of approximants, and the contact gap is zero.

notes.text:
Fix a finite pure positive balanced rational graph globally embedded in N_R, actual positive real edge weights w_e, and ACTUAL gamma in PA_R∩PC_q positive at infinity, with arbitrary real coefficients on finite rational geometry. Put K_v={lambda≥0:sum lambda_e u_e/v=0}; w_v is strictly positive. Insert a rational bivalent vertex on vertex-free lines. Then every u in C_b has a real-regularizable actual envelope, and contact for all these obstacles holds iff K_v=R_+w_v at every vertex.

Continuous printed-PC functions are convex on each edge by rational-endpoint approximation. At a vertex, small rational germ endpoints and the actual positive-weight PCC give a nonnegative weighted sum of secant quotients. Each quotient has a finite upper bound and decreases toward a finite or negative-infinite derivative. Positivity of every weight excludes negative-infinite limits. All relation costs of the finite derivative vector are nonnegative. Finite duality supplies vertex supports; convex edge derivatives supply interior supports. Conversely these supports prove PCC.

On an end, gamma(t)=g_e t+c_e after rational T_e, g_e>0. Bounded relative difference and convexity force f's limiting slope to be g_e. Thus f−g_e t is nonincreasing, bounded and has a finite limit. At sufficiently large rational S_e, replacing the tail by the line through f(S_e) of actual slope g_e approximates from above uniformly. Interpolate actual real values of f on fine rational meshes of bounded edges and compact end portions. Chord slopes are monotone and each outgoing vertex chord slope is at least the true derivative, preserving every nonnegative relation inequality. Shared values remain continuous, carrying positions are rational, and tail slopes are the actual reference slopes. Hence these are genuine relative PA_R PC approximants even with irrational coefficients. Rational constant additions yield a decreasing sequence. R230 supplies continuity and bounded relative difference for every unrestricted C_b envelope; this approximation proves its operator-domain antecedent.

The genuine raw completion is Delta f=sum_v(sum_e w_e d_v,e)delta_v+sum_e w_e d(f'_+) on edge interiors, in primitive coordinates. Monotone right-continuous derivatives define Stieltjes measures through positive test sums and the Radon construction in n4. Vertex coefficients are nonnegative. Bounded-edge interior masses cancel endpoint derivative contributions; each end leaves w_e g_e. Thus total mass is M=sum_ends w_e g_e=deg(gamma). The formula agrees with actual primitive PA recursion, including artificial zero vertices, and with literal completion wherever its separate antecedent holds.

Compact rational PA tests satisfy integral psi Delta f=integral f Delta psi by Stieltjes IBP, secant Riemann bounds and telescoping vertex terms. Consequently evaluation differences are at most TV(Delta psi)||f−h||. Controlled-support density proves sequence independence and GLOBAL vague uniform continuity. For EACH FIXED C with ||f−gamma||≤C, convexity gives f'_+(T_e+R)≥g_e−2C/R. Every completed output in that family has tail outside the compact core at most (2C/R)sum_endweights. Also integral H Delta f≤2CM+J, H=gamma+c≥0, J=integral H Delta gamma. For irrational references, q_j=max(gamma−j,−c) is not asserted rational PA: proved graph approximation supplies its genuine domain first, then IBP passes from finite approximants. Uniform families have a common C, proving all C_b convergence. Weak C_b continuity uses a radius-one neighborhood; weak/BL uniform continuity is restricted to each fixed-C family. M=0 is handled separately.

For contact sufficiency, a short chord replacement in a noncontact edge interval stays below the continuous obstacle gap and preserves convex glue, vertex inequalities and growth. Maximality forces local affinity there, so curvature mass vanishes. At a noncontact vertex with positive atom, the one-ray condition makes every nonzero relation cost positive. The corrected floor separation applies to its finite derivative vector. Convexity extends the strict floor bound without a PA germ. A small raised affine maximum with an unchanged collar contradicts maximality. Thus the positive measure is supported on contact and the exact bounded-gap integral is zero.

For necessity, dim K_v>1 gives a rational extreme relation omitting some coordinate e0; a fully positive extreme would admit two-sided kernel perturbations. The germ with slope 1 on e0 and 0 elsewhere is PC, flat on that relation and has actual mass w_e0>0. Realize it with the actual possibly irrational reference using a continuous slow-norm maximum and a strict collar. This intermediate maximum is not declared rational PA or assigned a measure. Apply the PROVED graph chord construction, keeping first rational samples inside the unchanged linear germ. The resulting actual relative PA_R function F has the same flat relation and mass delta w_e0>0. Only then use n2's exact PA roof: the bounded real PA obstacle has unrestricted envelope F and contact −R delta w_e0<0. No irrational PA maximum closure is assumed.

Finite evidence includes the rational cross with weights 1,1,3/2,3/2 and actual irrational affine perturbations alpha=sqrt(2)/4, beta=sqrt(3)/4. Squared values 1/8 and 3/16 certify positive reference slopes; affine terms cancel in relations. Reference mass is 5, compatible endpoint origin mass 2 and radius-1/4 contact −1/2. These checks corroborate the proof, not its universal claims.
